questions.solution: Correct answer: 0.

questions.text: Two identical particles, one initially at rest, undergo a perfectly elastic collision. In the laboratory frame, what is the angle between their final velocity vectors?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 90°.

questions.text: A driven harmonic oscillator at resonance is subjected to a driving force F(t) = F₀ cos ωt. The steady-state velocity amplitude is v₀. What is the average power delivered by the driving force over one cycle?
questions.solution: Correct answer: ½ F₀ v₀.

questions.text: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping down an incline. What fraction of its total kinetic energy is rotational?
questions.solution: Correct answer: 1/3.

questions.text: A small block is released from rest on a frictionless track that leads into a vertical circular loop of radius R. The minimum release height above the bottom of the loop required to complete the loop is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 2.5R.

questions.text: In an ideal pulley system with velocity ratio 4, a load of 800 N is lifted at a constant speed of 0.5 m/s. The power input required is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 400 W.

questions.text: A rocket of initial mass m0 ejects exhaust at constant relative speed u. According to the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, the change in velocity Δv after the mass reduces to m is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: u ln(m0/m).

questions.text: For a rigid body rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface, the work done by the static friction force is:

options.label: D
options.text: Depends on the direction of motion

questions.solution: Correct answer: Zero.

questions.text: In the work‑energy theorem for a system of particles, the change in total mechanical energy (ΔK + ΔU) equals:

options.label: A
options.text: Work done by all external forces

options.label: B
options.text: Work done by external non‑conservative forces

options.label: C
options.text: Work done by internal conservative forces

options.label: D
options.text: Work done by internal non‑conservative forces

questions.solution: Correct answer: Work done by external non‑conservative forces.

questions.text: When applying the work‑energy theorem to a rocket that ejects mass, the kinetic energy of the ejected mass must be:

options.label: A
options.text: Ignored because it leaves the system

options.label: B
options.text: Included in the total kinetic energy of the system

options.label: C
options.text: Subtracted from the rocket’s kinetic energy

options.label: D
options.text: Treated as potential energy of the fuel

questions.solution: Correct answer: Included in the total kinetic energy of the system.

questions.text: To apply the principle of virtual work to a system with non‑holonomic constraints, one must:

options.label: D
options.text: Assume the system is in static equilibrium

questions.solution: Correct answer: Use Lagrange multipliers.

questions.text: In a DC motor, the difference between the electrical input power V I and the mechanical power developed τ ω is:

options.label: A
options.text: Stored as magnetic energy in the inductance

options.label: D
options.text: Radiated as heat from bearing friction

questions.solution: Correct answer: Dissipated as copper loss I²R.

questions.text: A bar of length L, cross‑sectional area A and Young’s modulus E is subjected to a gradually applied force F. The strain energy stored in the bar is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: F²L/(2AE).

questions.text: In Lagrangian mechanics, the generalized force Q_k corresponding to a conservative force derived from a potential V(q) is given by:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Q_k = ∂V/∂q_k.

questions.text: In an AC circuit, the apparent power S is related to the real power P and reactive power Q by:
questions.solution: Correct answer: S = P + Q.

questions.text: Which overpotential becomes significant at high current densities due to depletion of reactants at the electrode surface?
questions.solution: Correct answer: Concentration overpotential.

questions.text: For steady incompressible flow in a pipe, the Darcy–Weisbach formula gives the head loss h_L due to friction as:
questions.solution: Correct answer: h_L = f (L/D) v²/(2g).

questions.text: The relativistic kinetic energy of a particle of rest mass m moving at speed v is K = (γ − 1) m c². At low speeds (v ≪ c) this expression reduces to which classical form?

options.label: C
options.text: ½ m v² + ½ m c²

questions.solution: Correct answer: ½ m v².

questions.text: In a reference frame rotating with constant angular velocity ω, the Coriolis force on a particle of mass m moving with velocity v' is F_Cor = 2 m ω × v'. The work done by this force over any displacement is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Zero.

questions.text: According to the Poynting theorem, the rate at which electromagnetic fields do work on charges in a volume is ∫ J·E dV. The magnetic force q v × B does no work on a free charge because:

options.label: A
options.text: It is always perpendicular to the velocity

questions.solution: Correct answer: It is always perpendicular to the velocity.

questions.text: In the sign convention used in physics and chemistry for the first law of thermodynamics, ΔU = Q − W, the term W represents:
questions.solution: Correct answer: Work done by the system.

questions.text: Two identical masses m are connected by three identical springs of stiffness k in a line with fixed ends. The normal‑mode frequencies are ω₁ = √(k/m) and ω₂ = √(3k/m). If only one mass is displaced initially, the period of complete energy transfer from that mass to the other is:
questions.solution: Correct answer: 2π/(ω₂ − ω₁).

questions.text: In a hyperelastic material, the stress power density σ_ij D_ij equals:

options.label: A
options.text: rate of change of kinetic energy

options.label: B
options.text: material time derivative of strain energy density W

questions.solution: Correct answer: material time derivative of strain energy density W.
